ei.subject: 수능특강Light

fullPassage: But there are whole areas of human behavior where standard policies are particularly ill-suited. To achieve behavior change, the government could well choose ‘hard’ measures such as regulations, mandates, and bans, which force citizens and corporations to adopt or avoid certain behaviors. For instance, in the UK it is an offence to smoke in certain designated public places. ( ) The prospect of paying a steep fine certainly stops many people from violating this regulation. ( ) Hard measures are usually employed when behavior is seen to be harmful to society and needs to be avoided. ( ) For example, getting people to eat more healthy food, exercise more, drink less, and so forth. ( ) To use coercive means to effect change in these areas would not be politically practical and would probably not be effective in any case. ( ) In such areas, the other option in the government’s toolbox is to rely on ‘soft’ measures, such as voluntary agreements which do not incur a penalty if violated.

questions.passage: But there are whole areas of human behavior where standard policies are particularly ill-suited. To achieve behavior change, the government could well choose ‘hard’ measures such as regulations, mandates, and bans, which force citizens and corporations to (A)[adopt / abandon] or avoid certain behaviors. For instance, in the UK it is an offence to smoke in certain designated public places. ( ) The prospect of paying a steep fine certainly stops many people from violating this regulation. ( ) Hard measures are usually employed when behavior is seen to be (B)[harmful / beneficial] to society and needs to be avoided. ( ) For example, getting people to eat more healthy food, exercise more, drink less, and so forth. ( ) To use coercive means to effect change in these areas would not be politically practical and would probably not be effective in any case. ( ) In such areas, the other option in the government’s toolbox is to rely on ‘soft’ measures, such as (C)[voluntary / compulsory] agreements which do not incur a penalty if violated.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 시민과 기업이 특정 행동을 '채택하거나(adopt)' 피하도록 강제한다. 행동이 사회에 '유해한(harmful)' 것으로 여겨질 때 강경 조치가 사용된다. 정부의 다른 선택지는 '자발적(voluntary)' 합의에 의존하는 것이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① abandon(버리다)은 원문 adopt(채택하다)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② beneficial(유익한)은 원문 harmful(유해한)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ③ adopt — harmful — voluntary: 원문 일치
❌ ④ compulsory(강제적인)는 원문 voluntary(자발적인)의 반의어로 부적절

questions.passage: But there are whole areas of human behavior where standard policies are particularly ill-suited. To achieve behavior change, the government could well choose ‘hard’ measures such as regulations, mandates, and bans, which force citizens and corporations to adopt or avoid certain behaviors. For instance, in the UK it is an offence to smoke in certain (A)[designated / unspecified] public places. ( ) The prospect of paying a steep fine certainly stops many people from violating this regulation. ( ) Hard measures are usually employed when behavior is seen to be harmful to society and needs to be avoided. ( ) For example, getting people to eat more healthy food, exercise more, drink less, and so forth. ( ) To use (B)[coercive / permissive] means to effect change in these areas would not be politically practical and would probably not be effective in any case. ( ) In such areas, the other option in the government’s toolbox is to rely on ‘soft’ measures, such as voluntary agreements which do not (C)[incur / avoid] a penalty if violated.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 특정 '지정된(designated)' 공공장소에서 흡연이 범법이다. '강압적인(coercive)' 수단을 사용하는 것은 정치적으로 실용적이지 않다. 위반해도 벌금을 '초래하지(incur)' 않는 자발적 합의.
det.analysis:
✅ ① designated — coercive — incur: 원문 일치
❌ ② unspecified(불특정한)는 원문 designated(지정된)의 반의어
❌ ③ permissive(허용적인)는 원문 coercive(강압적인)와 의미 불일치
❌ ④ avoid(피하다)는 원문 incur(초래하다)와 의미 불일치

questions.passage: But there are whole areas of human behavior where standard policies are particularly ill-suited. To achieve behavior change, the government could well choose ‘hard’ measures such as regulations, mandates, and bans, which force citizens and corporations to adopt or avoid certain behaviors. For instance, in the UK it is an offence to smoke in certain designated public places. ( ) The (A)[prospect / outcome] of paying a steep fine certainly stops many people from violating this regulation. ( ) Hard measures are usually (B)[employed / dismissed] when behavior is seen to be harmful to society and needs to be avoided. ( ) For example, getting people to eat more healthy food, exercise more, drink less, and so forth. ( ) To use coercive means to (C)[effect / prevent] change in these areas would not be politically practical and would probably not be effective in any case. ( ) In such areas, the other option in the government’s toolbox is to rely on ‘soft’ measures, such as voluntary agreements which do not incur a penalty if violated.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 가파른 벌금을 내야 한다는 '전망(prospect)'이 많은 사람이 위반하지 못하게 한다. 강경 조치는 보통 행동이 유해할 때 '사용된다(employed)'. 강압적 수단을 사용해 변화를 '이루는(effect)' 것은 실용적이지 않을 것이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① outcome(결과)은 원문 prospect(전망)와 의미 불일치
❌ ② dismissed(해고된)는 원문 employed(사용된)의 반의어
❌ ③ prevent(방지하다)는 원문 effect(이루다)와 의미 반대
✅ ④ prospect — employed — effect: 원문 일치

questions.passage: But there are whole areas of human behavior where standard policies are particularly ill-suited. To achieve behavior change, the government could well choose ‘hard’ measures such as ①<u>regulations</u>, mandates, and bans, which force citizens and corporations to adopt or ②<u>avoid</u> certain behaviors. For instance, in the UK it is an offence to smoke in certain designated public places. ( ) The prospect of paying a steep fine certainly stops many people from violating this regulation. ( ) Hard measures are usually employed when behavior is seen to be ③<u>helpful</u> to society and needs to be avoided. ( ) For example, getting people to eat more healthy food, exercise more, drink less, and so forth. ( ) To use coercive means to effect change in these areas would not be politically practical and would probably not be effective in any case. ( ) In such areas, the other option in the government’s toolbox is to rely on ‘soft’ measures, such as ④<u>voluntary</u> agreements which do not incur a penalty if violated.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문은 harmful(유해한)인데 helpful(도움이 되는)로 바꿈. 강경 조치는 행동이 사회에 '유해한' 것으로 여겨질 때 사용된다는 문맥.
det.analysis:
✅ ① regulations(규제): 정부가 '규제, 명령, 금지' 같은 강경 조치를 선택한다는 나열에 적절
✅ ② avoid(피하다): 시민이 특정 행동을 '채택하거나 피하도록' 강제한다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ helpful(도움이 되는) → harmful(유해한): 강경 조치는 행동이 사회에 '유해하여' 피해야 할 때 사용됨 ←정답
✅ ④ voluntary(자발적인): 정부의 다른 선택지가 '자발적' 합의에 의존하는 것이라는 문맥에 적절

questions.passage: But there are whole areas of human behavior where standard policies are particularly ill-suited. For instance, in the UK it is an offence to smoke in certain designated public places. ( ) The prospect of paying a ②<u>steep</u> fine certainly stops many people from violating this regulation. ( ) Hard measures are usually employed when behavior is seen to be harmful to society and needs to be avoided. ( ) For example, getting people to eat more healthy food, exercise more, drink less, and so forth. ( ) To use coercive means to effect change in these areas would not be politically ③<u>practical</u> and would probably not be effective in any case. ( ) In such areas, the other option in the government’s toolbox is to ④<u>refuse</u> on ‘soft’ measures, such as voluntary agreements which do not incur a penalty if violated.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문은 rely(의존하다)인데 refuse(거부하다)로 바꿈. 정부가 '부드러운' 조치에 '의존하는' 것이 다른 선택지라는 문맥.
det.analysis:
✅ ① force(강제하다): 시민과 기업이 특정 행동을 채택하도록 '강제한다'는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② steep(가파른): '가파른 벌금'을 내야 한다는 전망이 사람들을 억제한다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ③ practical(실용적인): 강압적 수단은 정치적으로 '실용적이지' 않다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ④ refuse(거부하다) → rely(의존하다): 정부의 다른 선택지가 부드러운 조치에 '의존하는' 것 ←정답

To achieve behavior change, the government could well choose ‘hard’ measures such as regulations, ②<u>mandates</u>, and bans, which force citizens and corporations to adopt or avoid certain behaviors. For instance, in the UK it is an offence to smoke in certain designated public places. ( ) The prospect of paying a steep fine certainly stops many people from ③<u>violating</u> this regulation. ( ) Hard measures are usually employed when behavior is seen to be harmful to society and needs to be avoided. ( ) For example, getting people to eat more healthy food, exercise more, drink less, and so forth. ( ) To use coercive means to effect change in these areas would not be politically practical and would probably not be effective in any case. ( ) In such areas, the other option in the government’s toolbox is to rely on ‘soft’ measures, such as voluntary agreements which do not incur a ④<u>penalty</u> if violated.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문은 ill-suited(부적합한)인데 well-suited(적합한)로 바꿈. 표준 정책이 '특히 부적합한' 분야가 있다는 글의 도입 문맥.
det.analysis:
❌ ① well-suited(적합한) → ill-suited(부적합한): 글이 soft measures가 필요한 이유를 설명하므로, 표준 정책이 '부적합한' 영역이 있다는 도입이 맞음 ←정답
✅ ② mandates(명령): 규제, '명령', 금지 같은 강경 조치의 나열에 적절
✅ ③ violating(위반하는): 많은 사람이 이 규제를 '위반하지' 않도록 억제한다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ penalty(벌칙): 위반해도 '벌칙'이 발생하지 않는 자발적 합의라는 문맥에 적절

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 범법 행위(offence). 영국에서 특정 공공장소에서 흡연하는 것은 '범법 행위'라는 구체적 사례.

( ) For example, getting people to eat more healthy food, exercise more, drink less, and so forth. ( ) To use coercive means to effect change in these areas would not be politically practical and would probably not be <u>effective</u> in any case. ( ) In such areas, the other option in the government’s toolbox is to rely on ‘soft’ measures, such as voluntary agreements which do not incur a penalty if violated.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>effective</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: effective(효과적인) ↔ futile(소용없는, 헛된).
det.analysis:
✅ ① futile(소용없는): effective의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ② powerful(강력한): effective의 유의어에 가까움
❌ ③ popular(인기 있는): 효과성과 다른 의미축
❌ ④ relevant(관련 있는): 효과성과 다른 의미축

questions.passage:
(A) The new law will take <u>effect</u> starting next January. The medicine had no <u>effect</u> on his condition.

(B) To use coercive means to <u>effect</u> change in these areas would not be politically practical. The president tried to <u>effect</u> a peaceful resolution to the conflict.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 effect의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A)의 effect는 명사 '효과, 영향'. (B)의 effect는 동사 '이루다, 실행하다'.
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A)가 '이루다'이면 take effect의 명사 용법과 불일치
❌ ② 둘 다 '이루다'이면 (A)의 명사 용법을 무시
❌ ③ 둘 다 '효과'이면 (B)의 동사 용법을 무시
✅ ④ (A) 효과, 영향 — (B) 이루다: 정확한 품사 구분 ←정답

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "an official order or rule issued by an authority, especially to control people's behavior"

det.korean: mandate = 명령, 지시 (권위체가 발령하는 공식 명령)
det.analysis:
❌ ① penalty(벌칙): 위반에 대한 '처벌'이지 '명령'이 아님
✅ ② mandate(명령): 권위체의 공식 명령. 정의에 정확히 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ prospect(전망): 미래 가능성이지 공식 명령이 아님
❌ ④ agreement(합의): 상호 동의이지 일방적 명령이 아님
det.tip: mandate = 명령, 위임 (정부·법원 등 권위체의 공식 지시)

questions.passage: Hard measures are usually __________ (employ) when behavior is seen to be harmful to society and needs to be avoided.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

employ → ____

det.korean: 강경 조치는 보통 행동이 사회에 유해한 것으로 여겨질 때 '사용된다'.
det.analysis: are usually + _____ 수동태 구조. 주어(Hard measures)가 '사용되는' 대상이므로 be + p.p. 수동태. are usually employed = '보통 사용된다'.
det.tip: be + p.p. = 수동태. 주어가 동작을 '받는' 대상이므로 employed(과거분사)

questions.passage: The government could well choose 'hard' measures such as regulations, mandates, and bans, which force citizens and corporations to adopt or avoid certain __________ (behave).
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

behave → ____

det.korean: 시민과 기업이 특정 '행동(behaviors)'을 채택하거나 피하도록 강제한다.
det.analysis: certain + _____ 명사 자리. 형용사 certain 뒤에 명사가 와야 하며, 동사 behave를 명사형 behavior로 변환. 복수형 behaviors가 원문.
det.tip: behave(동사: 행동하다) → behavior(명사: 행동). certain 뒤 명사 필수. 복수형 behaviors

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 특히 부적합한(particularly ill-suited). 표준 정책이 '특히 부적합한' 인간 행동의 전체 영역이 있다는 글의 도입.
det.analysis:

❌ ② easily enforced(쉽게 집행되는): soft measures가 필요하다는 흐름과 모순
✅ ③ particularly ill-suited(특히 부적합한): 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ widely accepted(널리 수용되는): 정책의 한계를 지적하는 맥락에 부적합

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정치적으로 실용적이지 않을 것이다. 건강 식단·운동 등의 영역에서 강압적 수단을 사용하는 것은 정치적으로 실현 가능하지 않다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① not be politically practical: 원문 일치. 뒤의 'would probably not be effective in any case'와 병렬 ←정답

❌ ③ always lead to behavior change: 본문은 이 영역에서 강경 조치가 '효과 없다'고 주장
❌ ④ become the government's only option: 글 끝에서 soft measures라는 '다른 선택지' 제시하므로 모순
